items.title: Constant-Size Commitments to Polynomials and Their Applications
items.authors: Aniket Kate, Gregory M. Zaverucha, and Ian Goldberg
items.abstract: Kate、Zaverucha 和 Goldberg 提出的 KZG 多项式承诺可以把一个多项式压缩为单个群元素，并用单个群元素证明某个点值确实来自该多项式。该实现使用 Charm-Crypto 复现可信设置、承诺、单点打开验证，以及基于插值多项式和消失多项式的多点批量打开验证。

algorithmSections.title: KZG 多项式承诺、单点打开与批量打开
steps: Setup：随机选择陷门 \(\tau\leftarrow\mathbb Z_p\)，发布 \([1]_1,[\tau]_1,\ldots,[\tau^D]_1\) 和 \([1]_2,[\tau]_2,\ldots,[\tau^D]_2\)。真实系统中 \(\tau\) 应在可信设置后销毁。
Commit：对多项式 \(f(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}a_iX^i\) 输出常数大小承诺 \(C=[f(\tau)]_1=\prod_i[\tau^i]_1^{a_i}\)。代码入口为 `kzg.commit(polynomial)`。
Open：在点 \(z\) 打开时计算 \(y=f(z)\)，并构造商多项式 \(q(X)=(f(X)-y)/(X-z)\)，证明为 \(\pi=[q(\tau)]_1\)。
Verify：验证配对等式 \(e(C/[y]_1,g_2)\stackrel{?}{=}e(\pi,[\tau-z]_2)\)，正确性来自恒等式 \(f(\tau)-y=q(\tau)(\tau-z)\)。
Batch open：对点集 \(S=\{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}\)，插值得到 \(I_S(z_i)=f(z_i)\)，再用消失多项式 \(Z_S(X)=\prod_i(X-z_i)\) 构造 \(q(X)=(f(X)-I_S(X))/Z_S(X)\)。
Batch verify：检查 \(e(C/[I_S(\tau)]_1,g_2)\stackrel{?}{=}e(\pi,[Z_S(\tau)]_2)\)。实现通过公开的 \(G_1\) 与 \(G_2\) powers of tau 计算两侧承诺。

items.title: Constant-Size Commitments to Polynomials and Their Applications
items.authors: Aniket Kate, Gregory M. Zaverucha, and Ian Goldberg
items.abstract: The KZG polynomial commitment scheme by Kate, Zaverucha, and Goldberg compresses a polynomial into one group element and proves evaluations with one group element. This Charm-Crypto implementation demonstrates trusted setup, commitments, single-point openings, and multi-point batch openings using interpolation and vanishing polynomials.

algorithmSections.title: KZG Polynomial Commitments, Single Openings, and Batch Openings
steps: Setup: sample a trapdoor \(\tau\leftarrow\mathbb Z_p\), publish \([1]_1,[\tau]_1,\ldots,[\tau^D]_1\) and \([1]_2,[\tau]_2,\ldots,[\tau^D]_2\). In a real deployment, \(\tau\) must be destroyed after the trusted setup.
Commit: for \(f(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}a_iX^i\), output the constant-size commitment \(C=[f(\tau)]_1=\prod_i[\tau^i]_1^{a_i}\). The code entry point is `kzg.commit(polynomial)`.
Open: to open at \(z\), compute \(y=f(z)\), form \(q(X)=(f(X)-y)/(X-z)\), and output \(\pi=[q(\tau)]_1\).
Verify: check \(e(C/[y]_1,g_2)\stackrel{?}{=}e(\pi,[\tau-z]_2)\). Correctness follows from \(f(\tau)-y=q(\tau)(\tau-z)\).
Batch open: for \(S=\{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}\), interpolate \(I_S(z_i)=f(z_i)\), build \(Z_S(X)=\prod_i(X-z_i)\), and compute \(q(X)=(f(X)-I_S(X))/Z_S(X)\).
Batch verify: check \(e(C/[I_S(\tau)]_1,g_2)\stackrel{?}{=}e(\pi,[Z_S(\tau)]_2)\). The implementation computes both commitments from the public \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) powers of tau.

items.title: Short Signatures from the Weil Pairing
items.authors: Dan Boneh, Ben Lynn, and Hovav Shacham
items.abstract: Boneh, Lynn, and Shacham introduced a short signature scheme from the Weil pairing. BLS signatures hash a message onto an elliptic-curve group, exponentiate that point with the secret key, and verify through a bilinear pairing equation. This Charm-Crypto implementation demonstrates single-message signing, aggregate verification for distinct messages, and fast aggregate verification for a common message, while noting the need for rogue-key defenses in real systems.

algorithmSections.title: BLS Short Signatures and Aggregate Verification
steps: Setup: generate prime-order bilinear groups \(G_1,G_2,G_T\), choose generators \(g_1\in G_1\) and \(g_2\in G_2\), and define a hash-to-group function \(H:\{0,1\}^{*}\rightarrow G_1\). The implementation entry point is `BLSSignature(curve="MNT224")`.
KeyGen: sample a secret key \(x\leftarrow\mathbb Z_p\), then compute the public key \(pk=g_2^x\). The `keygen()` method returns `SecretKey` and `PublicKey`.
Sign: hash the message \(m\) into \(h=H(m)\in G_1\), then output \(\sigma=h^x=H(m)^x\). The code entry point is `bls.sign(secret_key, message)`.
Verify: check \(e(\sigma,g_2)\stackrel{?}{=}e(H(m),pk)\). Correctness follows from bilinearity: \(e(H(m)^x,g_2)=e(H(m),g_2^x)\).
Aggregate: signatures on distinct messages can be aggregated as \(\sigma=\prod_i\sigma_i\), then verified with \(e(\sigma,g_2)=\prod_i e(H(m_i),pk_i)\).

Fast aggregate verify: when all signers sign the same message, aggregate public keys as \(\prod_i pk_i\), then verify \(e(\sigma,g_2)=e(H(m),\prod_i pk_i)\). Real systems should add proof-of-possession or another rogue-key defense.
